General Plan Designations
The City of San Jose formulated and adopted a General Plan in 1976 which is intended to guide the physical development of the city through the year 1990. The General Plan designations for each CNRA are briefly examined below.
Alma CNRA:
The General Plan land use designations for this area closely follow the existing land use patterns: Medium and Medium High Residential in the bulk of the area, with Neighborhood/Community Commercial along the Monterey Highway frontage, and Light Industrial on the San Jose Avenue margin.
Alviso CNRA:
The General Plan shows Medium Density Residential uses for the area of Alviso Planning Area affected by the CDBG program. This designation allows for a density of 8.0 dwelling units per acre. The remainder of the Alviso Planning Area is a mixture of medium high density residential, industrial, and various open space categories.
Campus CNRA:
The Campus area is shown in the General Plan as having Neighborhood/Community Commercial along the westerly and northerly borders, and High Density Residential (12-25 D.U./acre) in the remaining area. This is consistent with the existing land uses.
Gardner CNRA:
The Gardner area is almost totally Medium Density Residential with a narrow strip of Neighborhood/Community Commercial classification along the Willow Street frontage and a small pocket of High Density Residential in the southeasterly corner.
Mayfair CNRA:
The General Plan designations in Mayfair generally parallel the existing zoning. Southerly of San Antonio Street are shown the existing school and park sites as Public/Quasi-Public and Public Park & Open Space, respectively. The rest of this portion of Mayfair is Medium Residential (8.0 d.u./acre) and Medium High Residential (8-12 d.u./acre) is the same distribution as the current zoning allows. Included in this zone is the existing industrial site, a fruit packing warehouse between Silver Creek and Jackson Avenue.
The area northerly of San Antonio Street is divided into three G.P. categories: a deep area of Neighborhood/Community Commercial along Alum Rock Avenue; a narrow band of High Density (12-25 d.u./acre) back of the commercial; and Medium High Residential from that point (approximately the Stowe Avenue/Sunset Court line) south to San Antonio.
